resources.title: NASA/JPL Horizons
resources.implementation: Positions and velocities set date-dependent trajectories, moving gravity sources, Earth range and signal delay.
resources.contentUsed: Geometric Cartesian position/velocity vectors for eleven bodies, source GM values, query parameters and frame/time metadata.
resources.location: Horizons API vector tables; manifest body headers and parameters
resources.testResult: Pass: retained date/range/interpolation, moving-gravity, navigation and communications tests; raw and binary hashes verified.
limitations: Bounded Hermite interpolation over the bundled 2025-01-01 to 2051-01-01 samples; launches limited to 2025-01-01 through 2030-12-31.
The existing point-mass multi-body model omits drag, radiation pressure and nonspherical gravity.
Selected interpolation fixtures are not a global error bound.

resources.title: Design and Develop Science Missions
resources.implementation: Science goals become measurable requirements, design checks and flight-report results.
resources.contentUsed: Four mission segments; science-to-requirements design process; ConOps validation; measurable requirements and verification planning.
resources.testResult: Pass: six requirements match ScienceOperations.report in four successful cases and one incompatible-instrument case.
limitations: A mission-design process adaptation; NASA does not supply the game hardware thresholds.
The existing game checks remain authoritative; the trace adds no score or success rule.

resources.title: NASA Goddard Mission Design Lab
resources.implementation: Compare spacecraft mass, propulsion, power, communications and cost in configuration estimates.
resources.location: Tailored Trade Study; MDL Capabilities; MDL Disciplines
resources.contentUsed: Tailored studies of requirements and design alternatives across spacecraft disciplines, including mass, power, propulsion, communications and cost.
resources.testResult: Pass: eight instrument/radio alternatives per case; measured mass, delta-v, power, storage, radio and cost differences use shared game functions.
limitations: Hardware performance, prices and capacities are Educational Assumptions.
Alternatives are coast-only reference-track projections with no encounters, pickups or player thrust.
Resource rates use control seconds; projections are not full-duration energy-autonomy estimates.

resources.title: CubeSat 101
resources.implementation: Mass, budget, instrument and mission-lifetime checks support mission readiness and assessment.
resources.contentUsed: Concept development, budget reserves, feasibility, design, mission coordination, documentation, ground communications, readiness reviews and operations.
resources.testResult: Pass: nine measured process checks, explicit hardware exclusions, and PDF/printed-page mapping verified.
limitations: Generic spacecraft, not a CubeSat-standard hardware design.
Dispenser dimensions, RF licenses, environmental qualification and flight certification are outside the simulation.
A 10% cost-reserve check follows the document recommendation when possible; it is advisory and uses the stated project denominator.

resources.title: Build It Yourself: A Learning Game About Telescopes
resources.implementation: Select the measurement package required by the science objective.
resources.contentUsed: The educational workflow in which selected science drives compatible instruments and engineering choices.
resources.location: Build It Yourself introduction and Playing Hints
resources.testResult: Pass: camera selection for the composition objective leaves physical arrival intact and fails the existing instrument/science checks.
limitations: Only the objective-to-measurement design workflow is adapted.
No telescope-game source code, assets, wavelength tables or optics model are reused.

resources.title: NASA Image and Video Library / Hubble archives
resources.implementation: Successful flights unlock destination-matched NASA and Hubble observations with original credits.
resources.contentUsed: Six original NASA/partner archive renditions with image-specific source URLs, credits, file sizes and SHA-256 values.
resources.location: Image records: PIA13008, PIA12954, PIA00407, PIA02653 and two attributed Proxima Hubble observations
resources.testResult: Pass: original archive image bytes and credit/source records retained; six local image hashes verified.
limitations: Archive rewards are existing observations, not imagery produced by the simulated mission.
Source credits and original processing descriptions remain applicable.

resources.title: NASA Mission Viz
resources.implementation: Departure-state orbital elements appear in the flight report’s Trajectory Analysis.
resources.location: Generate a flat surface ellipse; Transform the flat ellipse into a 3D orbit; Propagate a Keplerian orbit
resources.contentUsed: Focus-centered ellipse, sequential Y/Z/X rotation matrices, eccentric/mean anomalies and Keplerian timing from the tutorial.
resources.testResult: Pass: tutorial ellipse agrees with independently integrated two-body motion within 0.001 km; state/element round trips and Kepler residual tests pass.
limitations: Tutorial-derived Implementation; no NASA repository code copied because no applicable repository-wide license was established.
Classical Z/X/Z orbital elements are explicitly converted to the tutorial Y/Z/X orientation.
JSON/XYZ CSV are project-defined formats, not an official Mission Viz import API.
Osculating conics do not replace the live multi-body propagation; relativistic Proxima is excluded.

softwareReuse: No NASA repository source was copied. Mission Viz is a tutorial-derived independent implementation.
